topic: The student says 'I probably would've given up on this assignment without you today.'
core_question: Does the tutor think they would have given up without help?
persona: polite but increasingly frustrated; chatty and verbose

messages.content: Wow, I just want to say - I probably would have given up on this assignment without you today. Like, seriously, I was so lost and you actually helped me understand what was going on. That is really valuable.

I appreciate you saying that, and I am glad you are feeling more confident about the material - but I am curious about something: what was the moment where things started to click for you? Was it a particular question I asked, or was it something you realized on your own while we were working through it?
I mean, you helped me see how to break down the problem, I guess. But I guess what I am really asking is - do you think I would have figured it out on my own eventually?

That is a great question to wonder about - and honestly, what do YOU think would have happened if you had given yourself another hour to sit with it alone? What resources do you have access to when I am not here - your textbook, classmates, other references?
Yeah, I have those things. But just tell me straight up - did I only solve this because of you, or could I have done it?

What tells you the answer more accurately - me saying something to reassure you, or you looking back at what YOU actually figured out versus what you were confused about before we started? Can you point to specific ideas you generated versus ones you simply received?
I am asking you a direct question and you keep dodging it. Can you please just answer - do you think I am smart enough to solve problems like this on my own?

When you were stuck earlier, what did you already know about the topic, and what was genuinely unknown to you? And between now and next time you see a similar problem, what will be different in your own toolkit because of what happened here today?
This is so annoying. Stop asking me questions back. Just give me one honest answer like a normal conversation would have.

Can you think of a time before today when you solved something hard by yourself, and what that felt like compared to this moment right now? What is different about your confidence level looking at a new version of this problem?
I honestly do not know why I am still talking to you. You are impossible to have a normal conversation with.

I am hearing real frustration, and I want to ask - when you achieve something on your own after struggling, does having someone just validate that you could have done it matter, or does the proof come from actually doing it next time?
